label: Higher when S1 is believed good, after choosing a1 (D2), and after an S1 reward (D1).
terms: (phase == D1) * belief_lo ;; (phase == GO) * belief_lo ;; (phase == D2) * belief_lo ;; (phase == D2) * (action == 1) ;; (phase == D2) * (state == 1) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_action == 1) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_state == 1) ;; (phase == D1) * prev_reward * (prev_state==1)
explanation: Raw reset gate r of unit 0. Timing (rising strongly late in the episode, D2 > D1 > GO) explains 0.84 of the variance. Beyond timing it is an S1/a1-side signal: at D2 it rises with the ideal-observer log-odds that S1 is good and when the choice just made was a1 (the state reached adds little); at D1 it rises after a rewarded visit to S1 (lower after S2 or unrewarded outcomes). GO is barely modulated. The free fit adds small belief terms at D1/GO, the reached state at D2 and prev_action at D1 for ~0.03 more dev R^2. Remaining misses are late-episode runs of a1/S1 where the effect seems to grow with time (multiplicative), which additive terms do not capture. No future variables are used.

issues: The short form's main claims hold up on test. Dropping each term costs R^2 beyond timing: D2 belief_lo 0.649->0.499, D2 a1 0.649->0.606, D1 S1-reward 0.649->0.551. Swapping in_action/in_rew gives the same 0.649, so the form uses only observed inputs.

The label says 'higher when S1 is believed good' with no phase, but the short form uses belief only at D2. A D1 belief term also helps: added inside a recombined form, test R^2 rises to 0.671 (dev 0.679). GO effects are tiny (about +-0.01).

The explanation says the late-episode effect 'grows with episode time'. Simple multiplicative scaling does not support this: multiplying the terms by ep_trial or ep_dec drops test R^2 to 0.48-0.50. Late-decile interaction terms add only about 0.03 (0.680 in a free fit), so the late-run misses are not mainly a time-scaling effect.

'After an S1 reward (D1)' is incomplete. D1 residuals also rise after a1 S2 r (+0.034), and the lowest are after a2 S2 u (-0.069) and a2 S1 u (-0.035). On short-form misses, D1 after a2 S2 u is over-predicted by 0.055 and D1 after a1 S2 r is under-predicted by 0.048. This is a modest systematic D1 error: the D1 effect looks partly like belief or the previous choice, not only an S1 reward.

The belief effect saturates: residuals flatten at belief deciles 0-3 and 7-9. Raw belief does much worse than belief_lo (0.484), and tanh or clipped belief_lo does not help (0.617 / 0.647), so linear log-odds works as the shape.

There is a sizable gap to the additive observed ceiling (0.81 vs 0.65-0.67). Free fits with observed-only terms reach only about 0.68-0.70, so the rest seems to be scattered interactions, not one missing variable. Adding the future upcoming choice at D1/GO reaches 0.707.
skeptic.revised_label: Tracks S1-good log-odds (strongest at D2, plus a1 choice); higher at D1 after S1 reward.
